newsitem.title: USA: TI sees chip market up 10 percent in 1997.
newsitem.headline: TI sees chip market up 10 percent in 1997.

text.p: Texas Instruments Inc said Thursday it expects the global chip market to grow 10 percent in 1997 following last year's sharp decline.

"TI forecasts a moderate recovery in the 1997 worldwide semiconductor market of about 10 percent growth, following a decline of nine percent in 1996," the company said in a statement released prior to a meeting with analysts in Dallas.
TI said the market for digital signal processors and mixed-signal flash analog chips should grow two to three times faster than other areas of the chip industry.
Tom Engibous, TI's president and chief executive officer, said the company is well placed to take advantage of this year's market growth.

"We are in a very strong leadership position in the digital signal processing solutions (DSPS) market," Engibous said in the statement. "We're by far the number one supplier of DSPs and we've moved up to the number two supplier worldwide of mixed-signal/analog chips."

TI's chief economist Vladi Catto said the company's projection of 10 percent growth in 1997 is based on continued strength in demand for electronic end-equipment, a historically low level of customer inventories and lower capital spending as a percent of industry revenues.
